Ordinary block kriging

Source: R/krg.R
bkrig.Rd

Predicts the mean value over each block (an area such as a district) by ordinary kriging with point-to-block covariances averaged over the block, C(s_i, B) = (1 / |B|) int_B C(s_i, u) du, under the exponential covariance (sill - nugget) exp(-h / range), plus nugget at distance 0 (Schabenberger and Gotway 2005, ch. 4). A block is a box, given as a 2 x 2 matrix of its lower and upper corners (rows) and integrated on a regular grid of round(sqrt(nq))^2 points, or a matrix of the points that discretise it.

Usage

bkrig(x, y = NULL, v, blocks, nq = 25, nugget = 0, sill = 1, range = 1)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

v

The values: finite numbers, one per point.

blocks

A list of blocks: each a 2 x 2 matrix (rows: lower and upper corner, columns: x and y), or a matrix of two columns of points.

nq

The number of grid points of a box: one whole number from 1. The points of all the blocks (nq, rounded to a square, for each box) must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

nugget, sill, range

The covariance: nugget from 0, sill at least nugget, range positive.

Value

A data frame with one row per block: est (the kriged mean) and se (its kriging standard error).

References

Schabenberger, O. and Gotway, C. A. (2005). Statistical Methods for Spatial Data Analysis. Chapman and Hall/CRC, Boca Raton. doi:10.1201/9781315275086

See also

Other geostatistics: crsof(), krigcv(), lfspec(), okrge(), sglmx(), smixm(), spobj(), spsamp(), spxy(), trsurf(), vgemp(), vgfit()

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- cbind(x = runif(30), y = runif(30))
v <- p[, 1] + rnorm(30, sd = 0.1)
bkrig(p, v = v, blocks = list(rbind(c(0, 0), c(0.5, 0.5)),
                              rbind(c(0.5, 0.5), c(1, 1))),
      range = 0.3)
#>         est        se
#> 1 0.3357770 0.1852905
#> 2 0.7159535 0.2114923
